The three exceptional divisors.

prop:s5-equivariant-torus-knots:
Proposition S_5-equivariant torus-knot embeddings: the \mathbb{Z}_s and monodromy tests. Let \Sigma be a Riemann surface with automorphism group \mathrm{Aut}(\Sigma) = S_5 (Bring's surface). A torus knot T_{2, s} with s \geq 3 coprime to 2 admits an equivariant embedding into \Sigma if and only if

  s  \in  \{3,\, 5\}.

An equivariant embedding preserves the intrinsic cyclic symmetry \mathbb{Z}_s of the knot.

Two tests. The fibration of T_{2,s} has monodromy of order 2s. For odd s the monodromy group is \mathbb{Z}_{2s} \cong \mathbb{Z}_2 \times \mathbb{Z}_s, the two rotations of the torus knot taken together. The criterion above is the \mathbb{Z}_s test: it asks only that the \mathbb{Z}_s rotation be realised in S_5. The stronger monodromy test asks that the whole \mathbb{Z}_{2s} be realised, that is, that S_5 contain an element of order 2s. This holds if and only if

  s = 3.

Under the monodromy test only T_{2,3} passes; T_{2,5} fails because S_5 has no element of order 10. The \mathbb{Z}_s test is the weaker of the two, and a statement that a knot is S_5-equivariant should say which test it uses.

Proof Proof of s5 equivariant torus knots. An equivariant embedding requires \mathbb{Z}_s \hookrightarrow \mathrm{Aut}(\Sigma) = S_5. The cyclic symmetry of the knot must match a symmetry of the ambient surface. An injection \mathbb{Z}_s \hookrightarrow S_5 exists if and only if S_5 contains an element of order s. The orders of elements in S_5 are the least common multiples of the parts of integer partitions of 5.

See Table.

The realised orders in S_5 are \{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6\}. The condition \gcd(2, s) = 1 forces odd s \geq 3. This restricts the possible orders to \{3, 5\}. \square

The monodromy test. An element of order 2s with s odd and s \geq 3 must have order 6, 10 or 30 among the divisors of 60. An element whose order is divisible by 5 is a 5-cycle, of order exactly 5, so orders 10 and 30 do not occur. Order 6 is realised by a transposition times a disjoint 3-cycle. Hence the monodromy test holds only for s = 3. \square

Corollary. Among torus knots T_{2, s} with s \geq 3, exactly two admit cyclic-symmetry-preserving embeddings into \Sigma_4 (Bring's surface): T_{2, 3} and T_{2, 5}. Any other torus knot of this family either breaks the symmetry in the embedding or fails to embed topologically (Seifert genus > 4, or s \geq 11).

The stronger equivariant criterion retains only T_{2, 3} and T_{2, 5}. The knots T_{2, 7} and T_{2, 9} are topologically admissible but symmetry-broken.

Remark The \mu–p residual: two readings of a two-pin discrepancy, and what decides between them. The two admissible pins of the aether modulus q_0 — the lepton relation and the proton ratio — do not meet. The discrepancy between them is small enough to be read as a prediction and large enough to be read as a gap, and the framework's own evidence does not say which. The epistemic-status remark records which pin the computed values use and why; this remark records what the discrepancy is, what has been proved about any term that would close it, and which observations would settle its reading. Throughout, \hbar_q = 1 - q^{-1} is the categorical Planck constant, evaluated at q_0 unless another argument is written; m_\mu/m_e and m_p/m_e are the CODATA-2022 mass ratios; and \mathrm{Vol}(4_1) \approx 2.0299 is the hyperbolic volume of the figure-eight knot, a mathematical constant carrying no experimental input.

The datum

The calibration discipline pins q_0 through the lepton relation

  \frac{m_\mu}{m_e} = \frac{\mathrm{Vol}(4_1)}{\hbar_q^2},

and the Physical-Observations layer pins it instead through the proton relation m_p/m_e = 2\,\mathrm{Vol}(4_1)\,F_{\mathrm{Bor}}(q)/\hbar_q^2 - 12, in which F_{\mathrm{Bor}}(q) = \lvert \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}}) \rvert\,[3]_q!/q^3 dresses the same volume by the Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M of the Borromean braid \beta_{\mathrm{Bor}} = (\sigma_1\sigma_2^{-1})^3 in the three-strand Hecke algebra H_3(q), with [3]_q! the quantum factorial. The two solutions differ by \approx 11.6 ppb, the proton pin lying below the lepton pin. The lepton relation has logarithmic sensitivity \mathrm{d}\ln(m_\mu/m_e)/\mathrm{d}\ln q = -2/(q\,\hbar_q) \approx -18 at q_0, so that separation is the whole of the muon-side residual: evaluated at the proton-pinned modulus, the lepton relation exceeds the CODATA-2022 value m_\mu/m_e \approx 206.7682827 by \approx 211 ppb. Write t for the multiplicative correction the lepton relation would need, (\mathrm{Vol}(4_1)/\hbar_q^2)(1 - t) = m_\mu/m_e, so that to first order t is the relative excess:

  t \approx 2.1 \times 10^{-7}.

The CODATA-2022 ratio carries a relative one-standard-deviation uncertainty \sigma_{\mathrm{exp}} \approx 2.2 \times 10^{-8}, so t \approx 9.5\,\sigma_{\mathrm{exp}} and \sigma_{\mathrm{exp}}/t \approx 10\%. The reverse assignment — pinning on the lepton relation and predicting the proton ratio — leaves m_p/m_e low by \approx 2.4 \times 10^{-7}; since that ratio is known to \approx 1.7 \times 10^{-11}, the miss there is \approx 1.4 \times 10^{4} of its own standard deviations. The proton pin is the working one for the arithmetic reason the epistemic-status remark gives: a residual of fixed size costs least where the experimental resolution is coarsest.

Independence from the trace convention

The Markov trace on H_n(q) depends on a Markov parameter z, the trace of a single generator \sigma_i; the canonical choice is z = q^3/(q^2+1), and an alternative convention sets z = \sqrt{q}/(q+1). The residual is not an artefact of this choice, for two reasons that need no evaluation at the pin. The lepton relation contains no trace at all: \mathrm{Vol}(4_1) is a hyperbolic volume and \hbar_q is a rational function of q, so no Markov parameter reaches its arithmetic. The proton relation contains one, but the closed form it uses for \lvert \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}}) \rvert — a rational function of h = q - q^{-1} with integer exponents — is what the trace becomes under the canonical parameter and is not what it becomes under the alternative. The trace of any element of H_3(q) is a polynomial of degree at most two in z with coefficients in \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}], because the Hecke relation and the Markov rule \mathrm{tr}_M(x\,\sigma_2\,y) = z\,\mathrm{tr}_M(xy) for x, y in the two-strand subalgebra H_2(q) produce nothing else. Substituting z = q^3/(q^2+1) therefore yields a rational function of q with integer exponents, and its identity with the closed form holds for all q; substituting z = \sqrt{q}/(q+1) leaves a remainder carrying half-integer powers of q, which no closed form in h can absorb. Both pins already sit in the canonical convention, and a change of convention has nothing to act on.

Constraints on a correction

Suppose the lepton relation is the leading term of a series in \hbar_q whose first correction supplies the factor 1 - t. Three constraints on that correction are established.

Order window. If the correction is a single monomial \lvert c \rvert\,\hbar_q^{k} with a coefficient of small height, \lvert c \rvert \in [1/5, 5], then k \in \{6, 7\} (qou:QOU.BraidKnot.MuPCarrierOrderWindow.order_window, stated for every \hbar_q \in [0.098, 0.1] and every t between 1.8 \times 10^{-7} and 2.4 \times 10^{-7}). At q_0, where \hbar_q \approx 0.0991, the two admissible coefficients are c_6 = t/\hbar_q^6 \approx 0.22 and c_7 = t/\hbar_q^7 \approx 2.25; orders k \le 5 overshoot t by at least a factor of 7.5 and orders k \ge 8 undershoot it by at least a factor of 3.6. In particular the residual is not a one- or two-loop term of the asymptotic expansion of the figure-eight Kashaev invariant whose leading term is \mathrm{Vol}(4_1): when the expansion parameter is identified with \hbar_q, those terms enter at k = 1 and k = 2 with coefficients of order one and overshoot t by factors of \approx 5 \times 10^{5} and \approx 5 \times 10^{4}.

Bar parity. The muon carrier 4_1 is amphichiral and its invariants are fixed by the bar involution q \mapsto q^{-1} (the self-dual real-volume proposition); the framework accordingly requires the correction to be bar-even. This requirement is an argument from the carrier's symmetry, not a theorem, and every exclusion drawn from it is conditional on it. Under the bar involution the aether constant is not fixed: \hbar_{q^{-1}} = -q\,\hbar_q (qou:QOU.BraidKnot.MuPCarrier.hbarGen_bar). A monomial \hbar_q^{k} q^{\ell} is therefore carried to (-1)^{k} q^{k-\ell}\,\hbar_q^{k}, which coincides with \hbar_q^{k} q^{\ell} for all q exactly when k is even and \ell = k/2 — and, since n \mapsto q^{n} is injective for q > 1, for no other exponent pair (qou:QOU.BraidKnot.MuPCorrectionAdmissibility.bar_even_monomial_iff). So the bar-even monomials are exactly the powers of

  w := q\,\hbar_q^{2} = q + q^{-1} - 2

(qou:QOU.BraidKnot.MuPCarrier.hbarGen_monomial_bar_even), and the bar-even dressing of \hbar_q^{6} is \hbar_q^{6} q^{3} = w^{3} (qou:QOU.BraidKnot.MuPCarrier.hbarGen_six_bar_even_dressing). Measured at q_0, the residual over w^{3} is t/w^{3} \approx 0.163 < 1/5 and over w^{4} is t/w^{4} \approx 15 > 5: no single bar-even monomial with a coefficient of small height carries it, at any pin in the window [1.1099, 1.11] and for every order (qou:QOU.BraidKnot.MuPCorrectionAdmissibility.no_bar_even_small_height_monomial). Together with the order window this says that the correction, if there is one, is not a monomial of small height in either \hbar_q or w; it is a sum, or it carries a coefficient of genuinely non-unit height.

Entropy. The datum t is known to \sigma_{\mathrm{exp}}/t \approx 10\% — about one significant digit. The order-six coefficient window that experiment cannot distinguish from the central value is \approx 21\% wide, and a dozen constants of small height — rationals, quantum integers at q_0, and simple functions of \mathrm{Vol}(4_1) and \pi — land inside it. Matching a closed form to t therefore identifies nothing; only a coefficient fixed before the comparison can.

Structural origin. What is known about where such a correction would come from is this. The lepton relation evaluates a scalar knot invariant, the volume of 4_1. The framework's working assignment places the muon in the five-dimensional icosahedral representation, carried by the (3,2) block of the five-strand Hecke algebra H_5(q), and the electron in the (3,1,1) block, which splits under the icosahedral group into the two three-dimensional representations; the natural correction to the scalar relation is then operator-valued — a Wedderburn-trace factor attached to the muon's block. The assignment is a working hypothesis of the generation tower; the factor has not been constructed. The most direct realisation, a shift of the projector weight of the Markov trace between the two blocks, is excluded on magnitude: the shift it produces is of order one, more than six orders of magnitude larger than t, and it does not reproduce the generation ratio either.

The two readings

The datum admits two readings.

(R1) The bare relation is exact. At the proton-pinned modulus the lepton relation holds as written, and the framework predicts a muon–electron mass ratio larger than the CODATA-2022 value by \approx 2.1 \times 10^{-7} in relative terms, with a definite sign. This is a falsifiable prediction, decided by any determination of m_\mu/m_e at the few-ppb level.

(R2) The bare relation is a leading term. The lepton relation is the first term of a series whose first correction is bar-even and is bounded, not determined, by the order window and the parity rule above; the framework's candidate for its coefficient is the operator-valued generation branching, which it has not constructed. The residual then measures an unclosed term: it is a derivation gap, not a prediction.

Nothing computed inside the framework separates R1 from R2, because the object that would — the a-priori coefficient — is what has not been constructed. On outside priors R2 is the conservative reading: the CODATA ratio rests on muonium spectroscopy and the muon magnetic-moment ratio, and an error of nine and a half standard deviations there is far less likely than an unclosed term here. R1 is what the bare relation asserts when it is taken as written.

Discriminating observations

Three observations separate the readings, and one class of computation does not.

  1. A coefficient derived before the comparison — bar-even and consistent with the constraints above — that reproduces t establishes R2 and closes the gap. A derived coefficient that fails to reproduce t falsifies the series it belongs to, which would then disagree with experiment at its first correction.
  2. A determination of m_\mu/m_e higher than the present value by \approx 2 \times 10^{-7} — or, far less plausibly, of m_p/m_e lower by \approx 2.4 \times 10^{-7} — brings the two pins together and establishes R1.
  3. Confirmation of the present central value of m_\mu/m_e at a relative uncertainty \lesssim 2 \times 10^{-9} excludes R1 outright and forces R2, or a revision of the second calibration relation itself.

What does not decide is any fit that drives the residual below the two-pin separation — a coefficient chosen against the datum, or an integer tower tuned to the CODATA value. Such a fit models the discrepancy as signal, and the entropy bound says it carries no evidence: a dozen constants of small height fit equally well.

Scoring

The per-observable accuracy ledger scores m_\mu as the proton-anchored prediction it is under both readings: the mass m_\mu misses its target of one hundredth of its experimental uncertainty by a factor \approx 970. Nothing here changes that score. Under R1 the miss is the prediction; under R2 it is the size of the unclosed term. In neither reading is it compute imprecision: the separation of the pins exceeds the inversion floor of the hundred-digit recomputation of both pins by more than three orders of magnitude, and the internal agreement between independent evaluations of the same quantities is at the part-per-quadrillion level.

rem:elliptic-stability-locus:
Remark The nuclear degeneracy locus is an elliptic curve over the Bring's surface. The stability curve and the color fibration of Bring's surface share the same algebraic origin. The conjecture is that the nuclear degeneracy locus — the curve in the (p, A)-plane where adjacent nuclei have equal energy — forms an elliptic curve isogenous to the fibrewise color curve \mathcal{E}_z.

The two cubics.

The color elliptic curve (color elliptic) at spacetime ratio z is:

  X^3 + (z + 1)X^2 + (z^2 + z + 1)X
  + (z^3 + z^2 + z + 1) = 0.
  \tag{C}

The nuclear stability condition (beta-stability), under the substitution t = A^{1/3}, yields:

  t^3 - cpt^2 - 2p = 0,
  \qquad c = \frac{a_C}{2a_A}
  = \frac{\lambda_C}{2a_{\mathrm{asym}}}.
  \tag{S}

Both are cubics in one variable parametrized by another. The color cubic (C) carries parameter z (spacetime) and variable X (color coordinate); the stability cubic (S) uses parameter p (Coulomb charge) and variable t (cube root of mass number).

Genus comparison.

The stability cubic (S) is rational. Solving for p yields p = t^3 / (2 + ct^2), confirming genus 0. The color cubic (C), as a curve in the (X,z)-plane, has genus 1: its projective closure is the smooth plane cubic \mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{col}} of color elliptic. For fixed z it is three points, and the fibrewise curve \mathcal{E}_z\colon y^2=F(X,z) is elliptic, with j-invariant a rational function of z.

The physical stability problem incorporates the pairing energy \pm \lambda_P / t^{3/2}, distinguishing even-even, even-odd, odd-even, and odd-odd nuclei. The degeneracy locus is the set of (p, t) at which an even-even nucleus (p, A) and the odd-odd nucleus (p+1, A) have equal energy. With the p-dependent energy a_C p^2/A^{1/3} + a_A (A-2p)^2/A of integer stability and pairing -\lambda_P/A^{1/2} (even-even) and +\lambda_P/A^{1/2} (odd-odd), the condition E(p+1) - E(p) = -2\lambda_P/A^{1/2}, multiplied by A/(4a_A) and written in t and \bar p = p + \tfrac12, is:

  t^3 - c\bar p\,t^2 - 2\bar p
  =  \frac{\lambda_P}{2a_A} \cdot t^{3/2}.
  \tag{D}

Squaring to clear the half-integer exponent and substituting u = t^{1/2} (so t = u^2, t^{3/2} = u^3, t^3 = u^6) gives:

  \bigl(u^6 - c\bar p\,u^4 - 2\bar p\bigr)^2
  =  \frac{\lambda_P^2}{4a_A^2} \cdot u^6.
  \tag{D$'$}

This defines a degree-12 curve in (\bar p, u). Factoring out the genus-0 component (the pairing-free stability curve) leaves a degree-6 residual curve in (p, u), generically of genus 1.

Conjecture. Let \mathcal{D} \subset \mathbb{A}^2 be the degeneracy locus (D') reduced by the pairing-free stability curve (S). Then:

  1. The smooth model of \mathcal{D} forms an elliptic curve \mathcal{E}_p over \mathbb{Q}(q).
  2. There exists an isogeny \varphi \colon \mathcal{E}_p \to \mathcal{E}_{z(p)} to the fibrewise color curve of Bring's surface, where z(p) is the spacetime ratio at which the quadratic coefficient of the color elliptic cubic (C) equals that of the stability cubic (S) under X = t:
  z(p) =  -(cp + 1).
  1. The integer points (p, A) \in \mathcal{E}_p(\mathbb{Z}) correspond to the stability pairs: the mass numbers A at which the even-even/odd-odd degeneracy falls exactly on an integer lattice point.

Coefficient matching.

The stability cubic, written as a monic cubic in t with parameter p, is

  t^3 - cp \cdot t^2 + 0 \cdot t - 2p = 0.

At z = -(cp+1) the color cubic (C) becomes, with z + 1 = -cp, z^2 + z + 1 = c^2p^2 + cp + 1 and z^3 + z^2 + z + 1 = (z+1)(z^2+1):

  X^3 - cp\,X^2 + \bigl(c^2p^2 + cp + 1\bigr) X
  - cp\bigl(c^2p^2 + 2cp + 2\bigr) = 0.

Identifying X = t, the coefficients compare as follows:

Coefficient Color (C) at z = -(cp+1) Stability (S) Agreement
X^2 -cp -cp for every p (defines z(p))
X^1 c^2p^2 + cp + 1 0 never for real cp (discriminant -3)
X^0 -cp(c^2p^2 + 2cp + 2) -2p only on c^3p^2 + 2c^2p + 2c = 2

The constant-term condition c^3p^2 + 2c^2p + 2c = 2 has, at c = \lambda_C/(2a_{\mathrm{asym}}) \approx 0.0145158337 (the asymmetry constant of neutron prediction comparison), the positive root p \approx 736.8, far beyond the heaviest known element (Z = 118). The linear coefficient never agrees. So under X = t the two cubics share only their quadratic coefficient.

Affine obstruction. No other identification does better. Removing the quadratic term writes a monic cubic as Y^3 + PY + Q, and a change of variable X \mapsto \alpha X + \beta with \alpha, \beta \in \mathbb{C}, \alpha \neq 0, sends (P, Q) \mapsto (\alpha^2 P, \alpha^3 Q). Hence

  J = \frac{4P^3}{4P^3 + 27Q^2}

is unchanged, and two cubics related by such a substitution have equal J. For (C),

  P_C = \frac{2z^2 + z + 2}{3}, \qquad
  Q_C = \frac{5(z+1)(4z^2 - z + 4)}{27},

and 2z^2 + z + 2 > 0 for real z, so P_C > 0 and 4P_C^3 + 27Q_C^2 > 0, giving J_C > 0. For (S),

  P_S = -\frac{c^2p^2}{3}, \qquad
  4P_S^3 + 27Q_S^2 = \frac{4p^2(54c^3p^2 + 729)}{27},

so J_S < 0 whenever c > 0 and p \neq 0. Therefore no substitution X \mapsto \alpha X + \beta carries (S) to (C) at any real z; equality of J requires complex z. Matching "up to a Möbius transformation" would add nothing, since any three distinct points of \mathbb{P}^1 map to any other three. The isogeny in item 2 is therefore the whole content of that item. This obstruction is proved.

Physical interpretation.

If the conjecture holds:

  • The three color tubes (r, g, b) of the color fibration correspond to the three sectors of nuclear binding: volume (strong), Coulomb (electromagnetic), and Pauli (exclusion).
  • The fibrewise elliptic curve \mathcal{E}_z at spacetime z encodes the allowed baryon configurations at that point; the stability elliptic curve \mathcal{E}_p at proton number p encodes the allowed nuclear configurations at that proton count.
  • The isogeny \varphi connects them, representing the passage from single-baryon color structure to multi-baryon nuclear structure — the same passage that takes the proton (proton) from a color-linked triple to a nucleus (stable nucleus).
  • The stability pairs act as the integer points of \mathcal{E}_p — the (p, A) \in \mathcal{E}_p(\mathbb{Z}) where the even-even/odd-odd degeneracy falls on a lattice point.

Computational evidence.

The fibrewise color curve \mathcal{E}_z at z = s - s^{-1}, s = \sqrt{q_0} (Descartes elliptic curve), is:

  \mathcal{E}_q  :  y^2 = x^3 + 0.7087x + 0.8056,
  \qquad \Delta = -16(4a^3 + 27b^2) \approx -303.17, \quad j \approx 129.86,

with a \approx 0.7087 and b \approx 0.8056 its Weierstrass coefficients. Since \Delta < 0, the real locus \mathcal{E}_q(\mathbb{R}) possesses a single connected component.

Stable hadrons as lattice points on the stability cubic.

The stable nuclei provide the \mathbb{N}^2 lattice points (Q, N) on the genus-0 stability cubic (Diophantine valley):

  t^3 =  p(2 + ct^2),
  \qquad A = Z + N = t^3.

This curve is rational: p = t^3/(2 + ct^2). For each mass number A \in \mathbb{N}, the stable proton number p serves as the exact integer minimiser of the convex quadratic E(p, A) (integer stability). There is no approximation — the integer minimiser of a convex quadratic is determined exactly.

Pairing lift to genus 1 (open).

The genus-0 stability cubic accounts for all stable nuclei via lattice-point enumeration. Whether the pairing energy lifts this curve to the genus-1 elliptic curve \mathcal{E}_q — and whether the stability pairs \{2, 8, 20, 28, 50, 82, 126\} then acquire an interpretation as integer points of \mathcal{E}_p — remains an open question. The structural parallel between the stability cubic and the color cubic (identical algebraic origin in the Bring's surface) is unproven, and the coefficient matching above agrees in the quadratic coefficient only, with the constant term agreeing at p \approx 736.8, outside the nuclear chart.

Established results:

  • The stable nuclei represent lattice points on the stability cubic (exact, from the Skein binding Lagrangian).
  • The Descartes elliptic curve \mathcal{E}_q exists and carries the stated invariants (exact, from the color fibration).
  • Under X = t at z = -(cp+1), the color cubic and the stability cubic share their quadratic coefficient; their linear coefficients never agree (exact, by the table above).
  • No substitution X \mapsto \alpha X + \beta carries (S) to (C) at real z, since J_C > 0 > J_S (proved).
  • The golden ratio degeneration at q = 1/\varphi^2 holds (exact, from the (s^2 + s - 1) factor).

The full numerical computation is carried out at 100-digit precision.
